claims.text: The proposed alloy is equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi or a slightly Ni-rich variant such as CrMnFeCoNi1.2.
The as-cast alloy has a coarse dendritic microstructure.
The as-cast Cantor alloy is a single-phase FCC solid solution at room temperature.
The as-cast alloy has limited ductility.
Cold rolling to approximately 90% reduction will produce high dislocation density and grain fragmentation.
Annealing at 200°C for 30 minutes after severe plastic deformation will trigger B2 ordering while avoiding appreciable grain growth and TCP precipitation.
The processing route will produce grains smaller than 50 nm.
The processed alloy will contain a supersaturated FCC matrix and a metastable coherent B2 ordered phase.
High configurational entropy and Mn-Ni atomic-size mismatch stabilize the proposed B2 phase.
Nanoscale coherent B2 precipitates impede dislocation motion without creating brittle interfaces.
Severe plastic deformation refines the grains below 50 nm through dynamic recrystallization and grain subdivision.
Low-temperature annealing supplies sufficient mobility for short-range ordering because selected atomic pairs have favorable negative mixing enthalpies.
Keeping the annealing temperature low prevents equilibrium sigma or Laves precipitation and suppresses grain coarsening.
Nanoscale ordered domains suppress grain coarsening through Zener pinning.
The processed alloy will have yield strength above 1.2 GPa and hardness above 400 HV.
Suppressing brittle TCP phases and introducing dual-phase interfaces will improve ductility and strain hardening relative to the cast state.
The as-cast single-phase FCC Cantor alloy typically has yield strength of approximately 200–300 MPa and ductility of approximately 40–50%.
Annealing above 400°C destabilizes the proposed nanocrystalline dual-phase structure by causing grain growth and TCP precipitation.
Reducing the normalized Ni content below 1.0 favors BCC formation or sigma-phase precipitation.
The B2 phase dissolves when annealing exceeds 10 hours at 300°C.

contradictions.description: The composition is called specifically 1:1:1:1:1 while simultaneously being specified as having excess Ni, exemplified by Ni1.2; these are distinct compositions.
The 200°C treatment is described as cryogenic annealing, although the stated positive temperature is not consistent with the ordinary meaning of cryogenic processing.
The cast alloy is characterized as having limited ductility, while the baseline assigns it approximately 40–50% ductility, creating an unresolved inconsistency in how its ductility is characterized.
